purpose: Predeclare the exact set of PubMed retrieval candidates to be measured, per the governing directive's Step 32 causal-separation requirement: the PubMed live-API date-filter fix and the (new) deterministic query compiler are two independent interventions, and their effects on Recall must not be collapsed into one before/after number. This file is written BEFORE any Candidate B2/C measurement code is run.

benchmark_scope.note: Identical 22-case set Candidates A and B1 were already measured on in artifacts/v2/phase4_baseline_results.json (confirmed by enumerating per_case_results entries carrying a 'pubmed' key -- 15 PM-* cases + 7 MS-* multi_source cases = 22, matching that file's aggregate_metrics.pubmed_rag.n_cases_with_gold and pubmed_live_api.n_cases_with_gold, both 22). phase4_heldout (12 cases) is not touched, per the same protected-split discipline the baseline measurement used.

candidates.name: existing local RAG
candidates.query_generation_method: none -- full NL string passed directly to retrieve()
candidates.corpus_api_source: local: data/index/ (FAISS dense index + BM25 + 9,000-abstract/22,674-chunk corpus subsample)
candidates.ranking_method: hybrid dense (FAISS cosine) + BM25 sparse -> Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60) -> cross-encoder rerank
candidates.fusion_method: RRF (k=60) fusing dense+BM25 candidate pools before rerank; not a cross-SOURCE fusion
comparability_caveats: Not directly comparable to the live-API candidates on corpus freshness -- the local index has a known, documented STALE_INDEX gap (13,115->9,000 non-reproducible subsample; PM-LIVE-01/02 are deliberately post-corpus-build articles RAG is expected to miss).
retrieve() takes raw NL text as input, unlike Candidates C/D which use the compiled term -- this is intentional (RAG is not being re-architected here), not an oversight.

candidates.name: old live PubMed (implicit 2-year filter, raw NL query)
candidates.query_generation_method: none -- full NL string passed directly as esearch term
candidates.corpus_api_source: live NCBI E-utilities (eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov), no local index
candidates.ranking_method: PubMed's own esearch relevance sort (sort=relevance), no local reranking
comparability_caveats: Measured against the THEN-current tools/pubmed_tool.py, which silently applied PUBMED_DEFAULT_DATE_RANGE=2 years whenever the caller passed neither years_back nor date_from -- this is the BEFORE state for the date-filter fix.

Confounds two independent defects (silent date filter + raw-NL-text search term) in one number -- do not attribute the full B1->C delta to either cause alone; B2 below exists specifically to separate them.

candidates.name: fixed live PubMed, raw query
candidates.purpose: Isolate the date-fix's own contribution, independent of the compiler. Same raw NL query text as B1, same live API, ONLY the date-filter defect is fixed (already true of the current tools/pubmed_tool.py -- no further code change needed for this candidate, just a fresh measurement).
candidates.input: raw natural-language query text (case.query) -- byte-identical to what B1 used
candidates.query_generation_method: none -- full NL string passed directly as esearch term, exactly as B1
candidates.corpus_api_source: live NCBI E-utilities, current (fixed) tools/pubmed_tool.py::PubMedTool().search_pubmed(query) with no years_back/date_from override
candidates.ranking_method: PubMed's own esearch relevance sort (sort=relevance), no local reranking
comparability_caveats: Directly comparable to B1 on every axis except the date-filter code path -- this is the controlled A/B pair for the date-fix's isolated effect.
Still not comparable to A on corpus freshness semantics: a live-API call always sees current PubMed content, so PM-LIVE-01/02 are NOT stale-index misses here the way they are for A.

candidates.name: fixed live PubMed + deterministic query compiler
candidates.purpose: Isolate the compiler's added effect on top of B2 (which already has the date-fix applied). B2->C isolates the compiler; B1->B2 isolates the date-fix; B1->C is the combined, non-attributable total.
candidates.input: a real nlu.schemas.ResearchQuery produced by nlu.understand_query(case.query) -- the actual frozen Phase-2 NLU architecture (Cerebras qwen-3.8-27b, per artifacts/v2/nlu_frozen_config.json), NOT derived from the benchmark's gold_query_must_contain_concepts (using gold concepts as compiler input would leak benchmark answers into the query and invalidate the comparison, not just the compiler's internal logic).
candidates.query_generation_method: retrieval/pubmed_query_compiler.py::compile_pubmed_query(research_query) -- deterministic, entity-verbatim, no invented MeSH/synonyms, temporal constraint reflected only if explicitly present in the ResearchQuery
candidates.ranking_method: PubMed's own esearch relevance sort (sort=relevance), no local reranking
comparability_caveats: Directly comparable to B2 on every axis except the search-term construction -- controlled pair for the compiler's isolated effect.

An extra NLU extraction step (LLM call) is now in the pipeline before retrieval; this candidate's own latency/cost numbers include that step separately from the PubMed API call latency, per the gate plan's 'never conflate stages' rule -- NOT counted in B1/B2/A's latency, which have no such step.

If nlu.understand_query() fails structurally (schema_valid=False) for a case, that case is recorded as a QUERY_COMPILATION_FAILURE for Candidate C specifically, not silently dropped from the denominator.

candidates.name: RAG + Candidate C fused
candidates.condition: Build only if B2/C results show live PubMed (fixed, with or without compiler) recovering gold items RAG misses on a non-trivial share of the 22 cases (e.g. the PM-LIVE-01/PM-LIVE-02 stale-index cases, or any case where C's recall exceeds A's at some k) -- i.e. fusion is only worth measuring if the two candidates' error patterns look complementary, not merely if both individually work. Decision made and recorded in docs/v2/PHASE4_HETEROGENEOUS_RETRIEVAL.md AFTER B2/C are measured, not assumed here.
candidates.input: if built: same case query, both RAG's retrieve() output and Candidate C's live-API output
candidates.query_generation_method: if built: RAG uses raw NL text (as Candidate A), live leg uses compile_pubmed_query() (as Candidate C)
candidates.corpus_api_source: if built: local FAISS/BM25 index (RAG leg) + live NCBI E-utilities (live leg)
candidates.ranking_method: if built: documented explicitly at build time per PHASE4_RETRIEVAL_CONTRACT.md Section 5 -- never a naive cross-source score sort
candidates.fusion_method: if built: to be named explicitly (e.g. round-robin interleave with dedup by PMID, or a documented RRF variant) -- not decided in advance of seeing B2/C data
candidates.reranker: if built: none new -- reuses each leg's own
comparability_caveats: Not built reflexively; this row is a placeholder describing what WOULD be measured, not a promise it will be.

metrics_to_report_per_new_candidate: latency_p50_p90_p95_seconds (external API latency and, for Candidate C, local compiler+NLU latency reported SEPARATELY, never conflated)
metrics_explicitly_not_used: nDCG -- benchmark gold labels are binary (a PMID is gold or it isn't; gold_relevance_type is exact_id or concept_based-with-any-of-N-counts-as-hit, never a graded 0-3 relevance score), so nDCG would require inventing graded relevance not present in the data. Confirmed by reading gold.gold_relevance_type across all 22 cases in the manifest -- no graded field exists.

a single composite score -- per PHASE4_GATE_PLAN.md Section 4, no composite decides a winner; the priority order (correctness/recall > no systematic source failure > ranking quality > multi-source coverage > latency > cost) is applied narratively in the comparison writeup instead.
priority_order_for_winner_selection: 2. No systematic source failure (a candidate that starves a whole case subset fails this even with good aggregate recall)
4. Multi-source coverage (not directly applicable to a PubMed-only comparison, noted for completeness)
causal_separation_requirement: The chain is B1 (old, broken) -> B2 (date-fix only) -> C (date-fix + compiler). B2's own recall number is the date-fix's isolated contribution (B1->B2 delta). C's number over B2 is the compiler's isolated contribution (B2->C delta). The raw B1->C delta must always be reported ALONGSIDE both isolated deltas, explicitly labeled as non-attributable to either intervention alone, never presented as if it measures the compiler's effect by itself.
